summary: A 1948 CDF 809R enclosed tower on Boucher Hill in Palomar Mountain State Park, abandoned in 1983, restored 2011-12 and staffed by FFLA volunteers since 2012.

facts.design: CDF 809R design: 30-ft enclosed K-brace tower with a 15x15 ft octagonal cab (FFLA gives a 16x16 ft base)

staffing.status: volunteer-staffed by the FFLA San Diego-Riverside chapter during fire season; typically seven days a week

access.note: Open to the public as staff resources permit; typically May 1 to late November; drive-up access

visit.trail_note: Boucher Trail about 3/4 mile from the Silvercrest parking lot; one-way Boucher Hill loop road; summit observation deck is wheelchair accessible

facts.agency: California Department of Parks and Recreation (Palomar Mountain State Park)

events.note: First tower on the site; FFLA cites a 1991 CDF lookout survey, Friends of Palomar gives 1921
Replaced by an enclosed 30 ft wood tower with a 14x14 ft cab
Lookout and site transferred to the California Department of Forestry
Current CDF 809R tower built and placed in service
Aluminum siding and new windows in the lower living quarters
In service until 1983; abandoned after that
Ember from the Poomacha fire lit the roof; two state park employees put it out with a hose
Structural stabilization and restoration by CAL FIRE and DGS during 2011-12; Cal Fire spent more than $300,000
San Diego-Riverside FFLA chapter volunteers began staffing the tower; tower reopened in September 2012
Full refurbishment through the San Diego-Riverside FFLA chapter (Friends of Palomar date)
Reached 100% fire-season staffing; FFLA reports the same level every year since, with few exceptions
May 2023 (5/21, 5/23): repairs to the weather station sensor mast facilitated; FFLA funds for structural repairs

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give different years because they count different structures on the site. A lookout has stood there since the early 1920s (first tower, 1921 per Friends of Palomar and the 1991 CDF survey cited by FFLA), it was replaced in 1934, and the current tower dates from 1948. The story uses 1948 for the structure standing today.

NHLR dates the structural restoration to 2011-12 by CAL FIRE and DGS. The Ramona Sentinel reports the grand re-opening on September 1, 2012. Friends of Palomar says full refurbishment was completed in 2013 through the FFLA chapter. The story gives 2011-12 for the restoration, September 2012 for reopening, and notes the 2013 date.

FFLA says the tower is typically staffed 7 days a week from 9am to 5pm during the open period. Friends of Palomar says 9:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. until daylight time ends in early November, then 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. until the late-November closing. The story says the sources differ and advises checking first.

notes_for_editor: Core history (1948 tower, 1983 end of service, 2011-12 restoration, 2012 reopening, FFLA staffing from 2012) is supported by two or more sources. The 1921/1934 earlier towers rest on NHLR, FFLA, SDUT 2012 and Friends. The brief's events not verified here and left out of the story: the 2010 agreement with State Parks, the 2016 'opens' item (the NHLR link title only), the 2017 mast and leak work, the 2019 FFLA $300 grant, and the 2023 $300 door-frame grant. The 2023 year-end report confirms the mast repairs and structural funds but not the $300 grant. A 2017 Voice of San Diego search snippet (not read) gives 'Built in 1946'; this conflicts with NHLR and FFLA's 1948 and is noted only here. The SDUT 2012 photo-gallery URL in the brief returns 404. height_m is converted from 30 ft.
